items.ja: 煮込みハンバーグ定食
items.note: The cafe's signature lunch — a ground-beef patty simmered in a soy-sauce demi-glace, served with rice and a side salad; both the patty binder and the sauce are wheat.

items.en: Taco Rice (seasoned ground meat, lettuce, cheese and salsa over rice)
items.note: Okinawan-style ground beef taco seasoning over rice — the seasoning mix and any added sauce are the unconfirmed part for a celiac; the meat itself rules out vegan.

items.ja: キーマカレー（温泉卵のせ）
items.note: Minced-meat curry with a runny soft-boiled egg on top; Japanese curry roux is wheat-thickened by default.

A Thai-style coconut-milk curry on the same lunch board as the wheat-roux keema — ask whether this one is also flour-thickened and whether fish sauce is used before assuming it's lighter or plant-based.
Toasted bread, ham and melted cheese with a bechamel top — wheat and dairy throughout.

items.ja: ベーコンエッグサンド
items.note: Standard sandwich bread with bacon and egg.
Plain fried potato is naturally wheat-free, but a home kitchen this size almost certainly shares its fryer oil with breaded items — ask before ordering for a celiac.

items.ja: 前菜（ハンバーグ定食付属）
items.en: Appetizer plate (served with the hamburger set)
items.note: A small starter plate that comes with the hamburger set; contents rotate and are not itemised anywhere reachable.

items.ja: キャラメルバナナのクラフティタルト
items.note: House-baked tart with a wheat-flour clafoutis custard base; the cake case changes daily so availability varies by visit.
Wheat-flour sponge roll with pistachio cream.

items.ja: オレンジチーズケーキ
items.note: Baked cheesecake with a flour-bound base, orange-flavoured.
Green-tea flavoured wheat sponge roll with cream filling.

items.ja: さつまいものレアチーズケーキ
items.note: A no-bake ('rare') cheesecake, so it may skip the flour-thickened base other cakes here use — but the crust underneath is not confirmed wheat-free, so ask rather than assume.
Flavoured with roasted buckwheat tea (sobacha) but this is a standard baked cheesecake — the buckwheat is a flavouring, not a wheat-free guarantee; the base is still wheat flour.
Tohoku-style mashed young-soybean cream in a wheat sponge roll.

A milk-based set pudding topped with simmered black soybeans — puddings here are usually gelatin/agar-set rather than flour-thickened, which is promising, but it is not confirmed wheat-free; dairy rules out vegan regardless.
Reviewers specifically praise the careful brewing method; black coffee is naturally wheat-free, ask if you want it without added milk for vegan.

items.ja: 生姜味噌の生ハムシーザーサラダ（Half）
items.romaji: Shouga Miso no Namahamu Shiiza Sarada
items.note: House dressing is built on 関谷醸造場's ginger miso — miso can be barley-based, and prosciutto rules out vegan regardless.

items.ja: 信州産キノコのガーリックサラダ（Half）
items.note: Dressed with tamari soy sauce and frozen-then-thawed enoki mushroom — tamari is lower-wheat than regular shoyu but not automatically gluten-free unless certified; ask.

items.ja: 木の花屋漬物盛り合わせ
items.note: Additive-free pickles of Nagano heirloom vegetables from the Konohanaya pickle shop; salt-only pickling is often GF/vegan but the exact brine isn't published — ask.

items.ja: 彩り野菜の塩麹マリネ
items.note: Shio-koji (fermented rice-malt salt) marinated vegetables — shio-koji itself is rice-based, so this is a promising option, but confirm no soy sauce was added.
Boiled soybeans in the pod with plain salt — naturally wheat-free and plant-based.

items.ja: ウズラの卵生姜味噌漬け
items.en: Quail Eggs Pickled in Ginger Miso
items.note: Miso can be barley-blended (mugi miso) — ask which miso is used; egg rules out vegan.

items.ja: 野沢菜とチーズの卵焼き
items.note: Nagano's signature nozawana leaf-mustard pickle folded into a cheese omelette — nozawana itself is usually plain-salt, but the seasoned egg mixture is unconfirmed for soy sauce.

items.ja: しいたけのグリル～生ハム醤油豆のせ～
items.en: Grilled Shiitake Mushroom with Prosciutto & Shoyu-Mame
items.note: Shoyu-mame is soybeans slow-simmered in soy sauce, a Nagano home-cooking staple the menu calls out by name — built on regular wheat soy sauce, plus prosciutto.

items.ja: 信州産舞茸と長ネギのピザ
items.romaji: Shinshuu-san Maitake to Naganegi no Piza
items.note: Wheat pizza dough; served with a shoyu-dashi drizzle and shichimi on request — ask about cheese for vegan.

items.ja: 味噌シュウマイ～かんずりとたまり醤油～（4ヶ入）
items.romaji: Miso Shuumai — Kanzuri to Tamari Shouyu (4pc)
items.en: Miso Shumai Dumplings with Kanzuri Chili & Tamari Soy Sauce (4pc)
items.note: Shumai wrapper is wheat regardless of the tamari dip; kanzuri is a fermented Niigata chili paste, pork filling.

items.ja: 豆腐とアボカドの醤油豆入り春巻き（1本）
items.romaji: Toufu to Abokado no Shouyu-mame-iri Harumaki
items.en: Tofu & Avocado Spring Roll with Shoyu-Mame (1 roll)
items.note: Called out on the shop's own lunch page as suitable for plant-based diners — but the spring roll wrapper itself is wheat, so it is vegan, not gluten-free.

items.ja: 麹バターのポテトフライ
items.note: Fries tossed in fermented koji butter — the potato itself is fine but this is a full kitchen frying wheat-breaded items in the same station; dairy butter rules out vegan.
Made with large-grain Kawanakajima natto from Nagano; wheat wrapper, dairy cheese.

items.ja: しょうゆ豆メンチカツ
items.note: Panko-breaded fried mince patty studded with shoyu-mame fermented soybeans.

items.ja: 塩麹漬け信州福味鶏の唐揚げ
items.en: Salt-Koji Marinated Shinshu Fukumidori Chicken Karaage
items.note: Standard karaage — flour/starch dusted and deep-fried; tossed with an enoki-vinegar sauce.

items.ja: 信州米豚の酒粕漬けグリル
items.en: Nagano "Kome-Buta" Pork Grilled in Sake Lees
items.note: Pork marinated in sake lees (sakekasu) — sake lees is rice-based and generally wheat-free, but confirm the marinade has no added soy sauce.

items.ja: 塩麹レモン漬け焼きほっけ
items.en: Salt-Koji & Lemon Marinated Grilled Atka Mackerel
items.note: Whole grilled hokke fish in a shio-koji and lemon marinade — naturally simpler than the fried dishes, but confirm no soy glaze is added at plating.

items.ja: 発酵カレー（ランチAセット）
items.note: The house specialty curry, built on miso, yogurt, fish sauce, fermented butter and housemade vinegar layered together — a genuinely unique dish, but it is dairy, fish-sauce and roux-thickened all at once, so it is neither GF nor vegan despite the healthy-sounding name.

items.ja: 酒粕豚汁　～門前こがね味噌使用～
items.romaji: Sakekasu Tonjiru — Monzen Kogane Miso Shiyou
items.en: Sake-Lees Pork Miso Soup (Monzen Kogane miso)
items.note: Standard pork tonjiru enriched with sake lees; the named miso's grain composition (rice vs barley) isn't stated — ask.
Baked cheesecake with a wheat-flour base, flavoured with sake lees from the local Tamamura Honten brewery.

items.ja: ふき味噌チョコブラウニー
items.note: A savoury-sweet brownie flavoured with fuki-miso (bitter butterbur-shoot miso paste) — wheat-flour brownie base; check whether butter or egg is used for vegan.

items.ja: 白玉そばアイス～醤油麹黒蜜がけ～
items.en: Buckwheat-Flavoured Rice-Dumpling Ice Cream with Soy-Koji Black Sugar Syrup
items.note: Shiratama dumplings are usually pure rice flour (mochiko), which would be wheat-free, but this menu names them 'soba' (buckwheat) and the exact flour blend isn't published — ask; the dairy ice cream rules out vegan either way.

items.ja: エルダーフラワー糀甘酒ウォッカトニック
items.note: Amazake is fermented rice malt and naturally wheat-free, but confirm no barley koji is used; check the vodka brand for gluten status if that matters to you.

items.en: Soy Milk & Koji Amazake with Lemon (non-alcoholic)
items.note: A non-alcoholic soy-milk amazake drink — plant-based; amazake is rice-koji fermented and normally wheat-free, but ask to be sure no barley malt was blended in.

items.en: Foret Coffee (locally roasted, hot or iced)
items.note: Straight black coffee from a local Nagano roaster — wheat-free and plant-based.

items.section: おすすめメニュー / Recommended Lunch
items.note: Chilled soba on a bamboo tray with dipping sauce, as a lunch set. Ratio (jūwari vs nihachi) isn't stated on the shop's site; the tsuyu dipping sauce is ordinary wheat soy sauce regardless — not celiac-safe even if the noodle is mostly buckwheat.

items.en: Hot Soba in Broth Lunch Set
items.section: おすすめメニュー / Recommended Lunch
items.note: Soba served hot in dashi broth as a lunch set; broth is wheat-soy based and bonito dashi is standard unless asked otherwise.

items.section: その他のメニュー / Other
items.note: A kids' noodle set; exact contents not itemized online — ask staff. Base noodle is wheat udon or wheat-blended soba.
Hot soba topped with tenkasu, crunchy leftover bits of deep-fried tempura batter; the broth is wheat soy sauce based.
Hot soba topped with foraged mountain greens/fern shoots/mushrooms (sansai); broth is still wheat-soy tsuyu.
Hot soba topped with a raw egg, named because the yolk resembles the moon; contains egg so it's not vegan.
Hot soba topped with deep-fried shrimp/vegetable tempura; the batter is wheat and the fryer is shared.
Topped with tororo, sticky grated nagaimo/yamaimo — a sliding, slippery texture that surprises first-timers.
Hot soba topped with sweet-savory simmered beef slices.

items.ja: 大海老天ぷらそば（温・冷）
items.en: Soba with Large Shrimp Tempura (Hot or Cold, your choice)
items.note: One large fried shrimp tempura over soba, served either in hot broth or cold dipped-style — you choose.
Thick wheat noodles in hot dashi broth — unlike soba, udon is 100% wheat flour, no buckwheat at all.
Udon topped with abura-age simmered in sweet soy; the tofu itself is plant-based but the dashi is usually bonito.
Wheat udon plus wheat-battered tempura — double wheat exposure in one bowl.
Despite the "soba" in the name this is wheat ramen, not buckwheat — a naming trap worth knowing before you order.

items.section: 冷たいメニュー / Cold Menu
items.note: The classic cold soba on a bamboo tray with dipping sauce on the side — the everyday baseline order here.

items.section: 冷たいメニュー / Cold Menu
items.note: Zaru soba plus a full plate of tempura on the side.

items.en: Chilled Soba with Nozawana Pickled Greens
items.section: 冷たいメニュー / Cold Menu
items.note: Cold soba topped with Nagano's salt-pickled leaf-mustard greens (nozawana); usually plain-salted but confirm no bonito seasoning.

items.ja: サービスランチ（数量限定）
items.note: Choice of zaru or kake soba, plus a mini kakiage tempura-fritter rice bowl, pickles, and coffee or apple juice — a filling multi-course value set.

items.en: Cold Dipped Soba with Warm Duck Broth
items.note: Cold soba dipped into a separate warm broth simmered with duck and scallion — a seasonal favorite.

items.en: Duck and Leek Soba in Hot Broth
items.note: Hot soba served directly in broth with duck meat and leek; "nanban" here refers to the leek, not chili heat.

items.ja: 釜揚げうどん（冬期のみ）
items.en: Udon Served in Its Hot Cooking Water (Winter Only)
items.note: Udon scooped straight from the boiling pot into its own starchy cooking water, then dipped in tsuyu at the table.

items.en: Sweet Red Bean Soup with Mochi (Winter Only)
items.note: Warm sweetened azuki bean soup with a piece of mochi; typically dashi-free but not confirmed by the shop.

items.ja: 梅甘露（かき氷／夏季限定）
items.en: Shaved Ice with House-Made Plum Syrup (Summer Only)
items.section: 夏限定メニュー / Summer Kakigōri
items.note: Hand-shaved ice topped with the shop's own small-batch plum syrup — genuinely wheat-free ingredients, though made in the same kitchen as the wheat soba/udon.
Rice-brewed sake; traditionally considered gluten-free, but always fine to double-check the label for additives.

items.ja: 信州産100％リンゴジュース
items.note: Straight apple juice from local Nagano apples — naturally wheat-free and plant-based.

The everyday signature order. Made from the house's own "Kuichi" (九一) flour blend — 9 parts buckwheat to 1 part wheat, i.e. about 90% buckwheat, a lighter wheat ratio than standard nihachi (80/20) — confirmed via the shop's own Instagram bio. Still wheat-blended, and the tsuyu is ordinary wheat soy sauce, so not celiac-safe.
The house 9:1 soba with a side of tempura added.
Large portion of the house 9:1 buckwheat/wheat soba.

items.en: Shinshu Golden Shamo Chicken Hot Pot
items.note: A hot pot built around Ōgon Shamo, a prized Nagano heritage chicken breed — a heartier cold-weather order beyond the noodle menu.

items.en: Cold Dipped Soba with Free-Range Chicken Broth
items.note: Cold seiro-style soba dipped into a separate hot broth simmered with jidori (free-range) chicken.

items.en: Free-Range Chicken and Leek Soba in Hot Broth
items.note: Hot soba with jidori chicken and leek in broth.
A tasting-style plate combining three different preparations of jidori chicken with soba — ask staff to explain what's included.
A seiro soba variation featuring buckwheat greens/leaf in the dish; ask staff for specifics.
House specialty named for the Zenkoji sandō, the temple approach road the shop sits on.
The everyday cold dipped soba; price approximated from a crowd-sourced Yahoo Maps listing.
Same cold dipped style as zaru but served without the shredded nori topping.
Cold soba served with a side of tempura; price from a crowd-sourced Yahoo Maps listing.

items.en: Cold Dipped Soba with Tempura (Zaru Style)
items.note: Zaru-style cold soba with tempura.
Topped with sticky grated mountain yam.
Cold soba topped with grated daikon radish — a lighter, tangier alternative to tororo.
Plain hot soba in dashi broth.
Hot soba topped with tempura.
Hot soba with a mix of mushrooms.

items.en: Soba with Grated Yam and Raw Egg
items.note: Combines tororo grated yam with a raw egg on top — richer than plain tororo soba.
A style that spread from Kyoto: hot soba topped with a whole soft-simmered herring fillet in sweet soy glaze.
Hot soba in a Japanese curry-flavored broth thickened with wheat roux — double wheat exposure from noodle and roux.

items.en: Chicken and Leek Soba in Hot Broth
items.note: Kashiwa (an older word for chicken) simmered with leek over hot soba; price from a crowd-sourced Yahoo Maps listing.

items.en: Duck and Leek Soba in Hot Broth
items.note: Duck and leek in hot broth over soba; price from a crowd-sourced Yahoo Maps listing.

items.en: Cold Dipped Soba with Warm Duck Broth
items.note: Cold soba dipped into a separate warm duck-and-scallion broth.

Buckwheat flour whisked with hot water into a thick dumpling-like paste, eaten plain or dipped in soy/wasabi — closer to genuinely wheat-free if it's pure buckwheat and water, but the dip and shared kitchen equipment still need asking about.

items.ja: 黒カレー（信州牛ゴロゴロ）
items.en: Black Curry with Chunky Shinshu Beef
items.note: The cafe's signature curry, bulked with big chunks of Nagano beef over a dark roux base — curry roux here is virtually always wheat-thickened, so treat as containing gluten.

items.ja: 赤カレー（バターチキン）
items.note: Dairy butter-chicken curry; contains chicken and cream, and the roux is wheat-thickened.

items.ja: 緑カレー（ガラムマサラ・シュリンプ）
items.note: Shrimp curry seasoned with the shop's own roasted garam-masala spice blend; contains shellfish, and roux/thickening method is unconfirmed — ask.

items.ja: 選べる横町あいがけカレー
items.note: Pick two of the three curries above served side by side on one plate; vegan status depends entirely on which two you pick (none is vegan as-is, but ask about a veg option).

items.ja: トルティーヤチップス　万願寺ハリッサソース添え
items.romaji: Torutiiya Chippusu Manganji Harissa Soosu Zoe
items.en: Tortilla Chips with Manganji-Pepper Harissa Dip
items.note: Corn tortilla chips are usually wheat-free, but the harissa sauce's exact ingredients (soy sauce? honey?) aren't published — ask.

items.ja: 北海道産マチルダ種のオーブンポテト　万願寺サムライソース添え
items.romaji: Hokkaido-san Machiruda-shu no Oobun Poteto Manganji Samurai Soosu Zoe
items.en: Oven-Roasted Hokkaido "Matilda" Potatoes with Manganji "Samurai" Sauce
items.note: Roasted potatoes with a house chili-pepper sauce; the sauce base (soy sauce, dairy?) isn't published — ask.

items.ja: スパイス・マカロン（1個）
items.note: French-style macaron shell (almond flour, egg white, sugar) — naturally wheat-free, but contains egg so not vegan.

items.ja: キャレ・ド・みそ＆マカロン
items.note: A Shinshu-miso caramel square paired with a macaron; miso can be barley-based (mugi miso) and the caramel's thickener is unconfirmed — ask. Contains dairy/egg from the macaron and likely the caramel.

items.ja: クラシカル・パンケーキ
items.note: Standard wheat-flour pancake stack with egg and dairy — never gf, not vegan.

items.ja: 2つのスパイス・チーズケーキ〈バスクとクレームダンジュ〉
items.romaji: Futatsu no Supaisu Chiizukeeki (Basuku to Kureemu Danju)
items.en: Two Spice Cheesecakes — Basque Burnt & Crème d'Ange
items.note: A Basque-style burnt cheesecake (usually contains a little flour) paired with a lighter crème d'ange; both are dairy- and egg-based — not vegan, and treat the Basque half as containing wheat.

items.ja: スパイス・ジェラート（シングル／ダブル）
items.note: Dairy milk-and-cream gelato spiced with the shop's own blends; base is milk, so not vegan, and any cookie/wafer mix-ins are unconfirmed for gluten — ask.
An add-on chocolate topping (also sold retail as a boxed assortment); dairy content and any wheat-based inclusions are unconfirmed — ask.

items.ja: コーヒー（ホット／アイス）
items.note: Plain black coffee — naturally gluten-free and vegan.

items.ja: カフェオレ（ホット／アイス）
items.note: Coffee with dairy milk — gluten-free but not vegan unless a plant-milk swap is offered (not stated).

items.ja: 蜂蜜じんじゃーラッシー
items.note: Yogurt-based lassi with honey and ginger — dairy and honey both rule out vegan.

items.ja: 柚子香る豆乳甘酒（ホット／アイス）
items.note: Fermented rice amazake blended with soy milk and yuzu — dairy-free. Amazake is naturally gf as fermented rice, but the koji source isn't confirmed — ask if strict.
House cola syrup spiced with the shop's own shichimi blend; craft-cola syrups occasionally use malt or honey — ask on both counts.

items.en: Classic Seven-Spice Chili Blend, iconic red tin
items.note: The 1736-founded shop's original blend — chili, roasted sesame, orange peel, hemp seed, nori and, distinctively, local sanshō pepper and shiso, a different formula from the Kyoto/Tokyo-style shichimi. As a dry spice mix it has no wheat ingredient, but the shop publishes no allergen statement and the plant also handles a wheat-containing ramen shichimi — ask if strict about cross-contact.
The classic blend enriched with generous domestic yuzu peel. Same wheat-free-ingredients-but-no-allergen-statement caveat as the plain shichimi.

items.ja: 七味ガラム・マサラ◎缶 12g
items.note: Yawataya's own fusion product — an Indian-cuisine garam masala finished with their shichimi roasting technique. Plant-based spice blend; same allergen caveat as the other tins.
A darker, more heavily roasted version of the classic blend for a smokier flavor. Same wheat-free-but-unconfirmed-allergen caveat.

The jelly itself is a bracken/kudzu-starch blend, naturally wheat-free, dusted in roasted soybean (kinako) flour with kuromitsu brown-sugar syrup. The chain's own allergen line for this dish names soy (from the kinako) but no wheat — still ask, since no formal GF claim is published and the branch's exact recipe isn't independently confirmed.

items.ja: わらびもちお抹茶セット
items.note: Plain warabimochi plus a bowl of whisked matcha usucha. Plain matcha (powder + hot water) is naturally gf and vegan, but ask whether this set's tea is prepared with milk or comes with an unlisted sweet.

items.ja: 抹茶きな粉わらびもち　お抹茶セット
items.en: Matcha Kinako Warabimochi with Matcha Set
items.note: Matcha-flavored warabimochi jelly in kinako, same soy allergen as the plain version.

items.ja: 黒胡麻わらびもちお抹茶セット
items.en: Black Sesame Warabimochi with Matcha Set
items.note: Black-sesame-flavored jelly; the chain's allergen line names sesame here instead of soy.
Plain usucha (powdered green tea whisked with hot water alone) — naturally gluten-free; ask only if it's served with an accompanying sweet.
Plain black coffee.

items.ja: アイス抹茶／アイス珈琲
items.note: Iced coffee is plain and vegan; iced matcha may be prepared as a milk latte rather than plain tea and water — ask which.
Flavor syrups aren't published; some Japanese kakigori syrups use condensed milk — ask.

items.ja: 鎌倉わらびもち　10個入（桐箱入り）
items.en: Kamakura Warabimochi, 10 pieces, paulownia gift box
items.note: Souvenir box version of the plain warabimochi; same kinako-soy allergen note as the eat-in version.

items.ja: 抹茶きな粉わらびもち　5個入り／黒胡麻わらびもち　5個入り
items.en: Matcha Kinako / Black Sesame Warabimochi, 5 pieces (takeout)
items.note: Takeout packs of the two flavored jellies; allergens are soy (matcha-kinako) or sesame (black sesame) per the chain's own labeling.

items.ja: 釜あげわらびもち　6個入り
items.note: A softer, freshly-boiled-style warabimochi sold as a gift set; kinako soy allergen applies.

items.ja: わらびもち2個入り＋わらびもちバニラアイス2個入り
items.en: Warabimochi (2pc) with Warabimochi-Topped Vanilla Ice Cream (2pc)
items.note: Vanilla dairy ice cream topped with warabimochi pieces — the chain's own allergen line lists both soy and dairy; not vegan.

items.ja: わらびもちドリンク　浅川園のお抹茶
items.note: A milk matcha drink with warabimochi jelly pieces mixed in — contains dairy and the soy-allergen kinako topping.

items.ja: わらびもちドリンク　贅沢いちごミルク
items.en: Warabimochi Drink — Luxury Strawberry Milk (Yasuda yogurt)
items.note: Dairy strawberry-yogurt drink with warabimochi jelly pieces.

items.ja: わらびもちドリンク　鎌倉オリジナルブレンド珈琲ミルク
items.romaji: Warabimochi Dorinku Kamakura Orijinaru Burendo Koohii Miruku
items.en: Warabimochi Drink — Kamakura Blend Coffee Milk
items.note: Coffee-milk drink with warabimochi jelly pieces — dairy-based.

items.ja: 抹茶ラテ／ほうじ茶ラテ（わらびもちドリンク）
items.note: Milk-based lattes; not vegan unless a plant-milk swap is offered (not stated).

items.ja: 冬季限定　わらびもちぜんざい（白玉入り）
items.en: Winter-Only Warabimochi Zenzai with Shiratama Dumplings
items.note: Sweet azuki-bean soup with warabimochi and rice-flour shiratama dumplings. Shiratama itself is rice flour (gf), but this item was documented at another branch as an example — confirm it actually runs at the Zenkoji/Nakamise store and whether the anko has any non-vegan additions.

items.ja: ゴルゴンゾーラチーズケーキ
items.note: The shop's signature — Gorgonzola blue cheese blended into a baked cream-cheese cake on a wheat-flour crumb base.

items.ja: ニューヨークチーズケーキ
items.note: Dense baked cheesecake, a menu regular alongside the Gorgonzola version.

items.section: Cakes (seasonal, changes with the fruit season)
items.note: Wheat-flour pastry shell filled with seasonal Nagano persimmon; the fruit-forward tart lineup rotates through the year.
Some gateau au chocolat recipes use little to no flour, but this shop's recipe isn't published — ask before assuming it's wheat-free; contains butter and egg regardless.
A savoury egg-and-cream tart in a wheat-flour pastry case — one of the shop's few non-sweet items.
Wheat pastry shell with a sweet-potato custard filling.
A whole roasted apple dessert — potentially the safest sweet on the menu if served without pastry, but butter/sugar glaze and any accompanying crust are unconfirmed.
No-bake cheesecakes sometimes skip a flour-based crust in favour of crushed biscuit or none at all — not confirmed here either way.
Green-tea version of the chocolate gateau; same flour-content caveat as the plain version.
A fruit tart built on a wheat pastry base; singled out by a visiting blogger as especially good.
Fresh watermelon syrup over shaved ice — inherently wheat-free; confirm the syrup has no added dairy/condensed milk for vegan.
Citrus syrup over milk-based shaved ice — wheat-free but dairy, so not vegan.

items.ja: かき氷（生姜あずきミルク）
items.en: Shaved Ice, Ginger, Red Bean & Milk (summer only)
items.note: Sweetened azuki red bean and ginger syrup over milk shaved ice — wheat-free, contains dairy.
House-made red shiso syrup with soda water — naturally wheat-free and plant-based.
Note the house policy: the owner asks that a drink be ordered alongside a cake, so budget for both. Black coffee is fine for either diet; ask before adding milk.
Straight espresso shot.
Bergamot-scented black tea.

items.note: Cold soba dipped into a separate warm duck-and-scallion broth.

items.ja: 信州サーモンのてまり寿司ともりそば
items.romaji: Shinshū Sāmon no Temari-zushi to Mori Soba
items.en: Shinshu Salmon Ball Sushi with Cold Soba
items.section: 冷たいおそば / Cold Soba
items.note: Pairs small ball-shaped nigiri-style sushi topped with Shinshu-farmed salmon alongside a plate of cold soba.

items.ja: おやき（各種：野沢菜／野菜ミックス／つぶあん／かぼちゃ／丸なす）
items.section: 軽食 / Light Bites & 信州名産 / Shinshu Specialties
items.note: Nagano's classic dough dumpling, sold here in five fillings: nozawana pickled greens, mixed vegetable, chunky red bean paste (tsubuan), pumpkin, and whole eggplant. The dough is wheat-based unless stated otherwise, and the savory fillings are typically miso- or soy-seasoned — none confirmed wheat-free.

A chewy mochi-like sweet studded with walnuts; yubeshi-style confections are traditionally made with soy sauce folded into the dough, so treat as wheat-containing unless confirmed otherwise, and confirm no honey/gelatin for vegan.

items.ja: 生そば（5食入り・そばつゆサービス）
items.en: Uncooked Soba Noodles to Take Home (5 Servings, with Tsuyu)
items.note: Dry-packaged raw noodles plus a bottle of the shop's own tsuyu, meant for cooking at home — same wheat-blend and wheat-soy tsuyu caveats apply as the in-store soba.
Salt-pickled leaf-mustard greens, Nagano's signature pickle; usually plain-salt and wheat-free, but confirm no bonito seasoning was added before calling it vegan.
A packaged Shinshu confection built around beans; exact preparation (candied, coated, or baked with flour) isn't detailed on the shop's page — ask before assuming vegan or gluten-free.

items.en: Sweet Red Bean Soup with Buckwheat Mochi Balls
items.note: Warm zenzai (sweetened azuki soup) with shiratama dumplings made using buckwheat flour — a genuinely more buckwheat-forward dessert, though prepared in a kitchen shared with wheat items.
Standard Japanese lager; beer is barley-based and contains gluten despite being plant-derived.
Straight apple juice — naturally wheat-free and plant-based.

The everyday order. Tabelog's shop-description text states the noodle is nihachi (二八, roughly 80% buckwheat / 20% wheat) made from stone-ground local flour, with a sweet, clean-tasting tsuyu. The shop's own site (sp.raqmo.com) is currently dead with no Wayback snapshot, so this rests on third-party sources.
Cold dipped soba with a side of tempura; price from a crowd-sourced Yahoo Maps listing.
A smaller-portion version of the plain cold dipped soba; exact price not found in any source checked.
Crowd-sourced listings show a range of ¥650–850 for this item depending on date/source.
Topped with sticky grated mountain yam; hot or cold depending on preparation.

items.en: Hot Soba in Broth with Grated Mountain Yam
items.note: Hot broth version specifically, distinct from the shop's separate とろろそば listing.
Hot soba topped with a soft-simmered herring fillet in sweet soy glaze.
Hot soba topped with a mix of mushrooms; exact varieties not specified.
Topped with nameko, a small slippery-capped mushroom, in hot broth.
Crowd-sourced listings show roughly ¥1,350–1,500; meat cut/type not specified in any source checked.
Hot soba topped with pork; cut and seasoning not specified.
A specialty: chilled soba dipped into a separate hot broth loaded with juicy chicken, thin-sliced burdock root, and leek — reviewers note the broth holds its heat unusually well.
A seasonal tempura side of maitake ("dancing") mushroom — wheat batter, deep-fried, but no animal ingredients in the mushroom itself.
Tube-shaped steamed fish cake (chikuwa), battered and deep-fried — contains fish and wheat.

items.en: Sweet Dashi Egg Omelet (Owariya's Signature Side)
items.note: The shop's most-mentioned item across every source checked: a soft, sweet-savory rolled omelet cooked with a bold dashi, served on an ice-cream stick for easy eating, with grated daikon and soy sauce on the side. Contains egg so it isn't vegan, and the accompanying daikon/soy typically carries bonito dashi too.
A custard-style pudding flavored with roasted soba tea, not buckwheat flour itself; confirm dairy/egg content before calling it vegan.

Buckwheat flour whisked into a thick dumpling paste. One local write-up notes it can be ordered vegan/halal-friendly by asking for plain soy sauce instead of the usual topping — still confirm that soy sauce and the shared kitchen equipment are acceptable to you.
A complimentary crunchy fried-soba snack brought out while you wait for your order — deep-fried, so wheat-adjacent equipment is in play even if the noodle base is buckwheat-forward.

items.en: Raw Soba Noodles to Take Home
items.note: Dry-packaged raw noodles to cook at home, made from the same wheat-blend flour as the in-store soba.

This shop's own bestseller and the classic Nagano farmhouse dumpling: chopped nozawana pickle stir-fried with cabbage and carrot, wrapped in a wheat-flour dough and griddled/steamed. The shop's own ingredient list names egg, wheat flour, soybean oil and sesame oil — wheat AND egg, so not GF and not vegan despite the vegetable filling. Tabelog listed this at ¥150 (2010, likely stale); the shop's own site prices oyaki from ¥250 after a mid-2026 cost-driven price revision, not broken out per flavor.
Sliced Shinshu round eggplant with a sweet-spicy miso filling that runs when you bite in. Same egg-and-wheat dough as the rest of the line — not GF, not vegan.

items.ja: 門前おやき（きざみナス）
items.note: Chopped long eggplant folded into sweet Shinshu miso. Wheat-and-egg dough — not GF, not vegan.

items.ja: 門前おやき（野菜ミックス）
items.note: Cabbage, kiriboshi daikon, carrot, shimeji mushroom and aburaage fried tofu. Contains egg in the dough plus fried tofu (soy) — not GF, not vegan.

items.ja: 門前おやき（きのこミックス）
items.note: Shimeji, shiitake and enoki mushrooms packed into the dough, their own liquid doubling as seasoning. Wheat-and-egg dough — not GF, not vegan.

items.ja: 門前おやき（ラー油野沢菜）
items.note: The shop's popular nozawana filling with a shot of chili oil added, marketed as a beer pairing. Egg-and-wheat dough — not GF, not vegan.

items.ja: 門前おやき（ねぎ味噌チーズ）
items.note: Melting natural cheese with scallion and miso — the shop's own East-meets-West newer flavor. Contains dairy cheese plus egg and wheat in the dough — not GF, not vegan.
Lightly miso-sweetened pumpkin paste with a scatter of sesame seeds. Egg-and-wheat dough — not GF, not vegan.

Slow-cooked chunky azuki bean paste — the shop notes it's unexpectedly popular with visitors from Kansai. Anko is usually vegan on its own, but this shop's dough is egg-enriched wheat flour, so the finished dumpling is neither GF nor vegan.

items.ja: つち茂×八幡屋磯五郎「オリジナルおやき七味」
items.romaji: Tsuchimo x Yawataya Isogorō "Original Oyaki Shichimi"
items.note: A medium-hot custom shichimi blend made with the famous Nagano spice house Yawataya Isogorō, built to season oyaki and miso dishes — sansho pepper, seaweed and yuzu aroma. Dry spice blends are usually GF but not confirmed here; typically no animal ingredients.

items.section: 煮豆・豆菓子 / Bean Snacks
items.note: The shop's best-selling bean snack: crunchy beans in a bamboo-charcoal coating with a savory soy-sauce-based flavor. Soy sauce is wheat by default — not GF. Likely vegan but confirm no bonito extract in the seasoning.

items.section: 煮豆・豆菓子 / Bean Snacks
items.note: Large scarlet runner beans (hanamame) simmered sweet — likely with sugar and soy sauce; ask about the exact seasoning liquid for GF, and whether any dashi is bonito-based for vegan.

items.ja: 信州野辺山産　高原花豆（大）
items.en: Nobeyama Highland Scarlet Runner Beans, large bag
items.note: Raw dried beans for home cooking, grown on the Nobeyama highlands — plain and unseasoned as sold, naturally GF and vegan.

items.ja: 信州野辺山産　高原花豆（小）
items.en: Nobeyama Highland Scarlet Runner Beans, small bag
items.note: Same raw dried beans as the large bag, smaller size. Plain and unseasoned — GF and vegan.

items.ja: 信州七二会産　ひたし豆（鞍掛豆）
items.note: Kurakake-mame, a black-striped soybean grown in Futatsuai, prepared as hitashi-mame (soaked/steeped, usually in a light dashi-soy liquid). Ask whether the soaking liquid is soy sauce (wheat) and whether the dashi is bonito-based.

items.ja: 6種の信州りんごジュース(6缶セット)
items.en: Six Varieties of Nagano Apple Juice, 6-can set
items.note: Straight apple juice from six different Nagano apple varieties. Naturally GF and vegan.

items.en: Napa Cabbage and Broccoli Cream Pasta
items.note: Rich dairy-cream pasta built on Shinshu-grown napa cabbage and broccoli — the shop's own copy names the vegetables as locally sourced.
Ground Shinshu beef ragù, slow-cooked with aromatic vegetables — the shop's headline pasta.

items.ja: 牡蠣のペペロンチーノ
items.note: Chili-and-garlic spaghetti loaded with oysters.
Neapolitan-style crust made from the shop's own blend of Shinshu and imported Italian flour, tomato sauce, melted natural cheese.

items.ja: 信州味噌とクリームチーズソースのピザ
items.romaji: Shinshuu Miso to Kuriimu Chiizu Soosu no Piza
items.en: Shinshu Miso and Cream Cheese Pizza with Mushrooms
items.note: Shinshu rice-koji miso worked into a cream-cheese sauce, topped with mushrooms — check whether the miso used is barley-blended before treating the sauce as wheat-free-adjacent; the crust is wheat regardless.

items.ja: ニンニクとアンチョビバターのピザ
items.romaji: Ninniku to Anchobi Bataa no Piza
items.note: Garlic and salty anchovy over butter — savory, not vegetarian.

items.ja: クアトロフォルマッジ
items.note: Four cheeses finished with a drizzle of honey.

items.ja: ジャガイモとサツマイモのバタークリームピザ
items.romaji: Jagaimo to Satsumaimo no Bataa Kuriimu Piza
items.en: Potato and Sweet Potato Butter Cream Pizza
items.note: A meat-free but dairy-heavy pizza — good vegetarian pick if not vegan.
Classic tomato-mozzarella base with anchovy on top.
Over 200g of Shinshu-sourced venison patty with onion, carrot and celery folded in for umami, finished in olive oil; whether a wheat-flour or breadcrumb binder is used isn't stated — ask.

items.en: Venison Thigh Steak with Mixed Berry Sauce
items.note: 200g venison thigh steak with a currant-and-blackberry sauce; sauce may be flour-thickened — ask. A genuine local specialty: the chef sources the deer through a proper processing facility.
Chef Iwata's own house-smoked venison starter; curing seasonings not detailed.
Slow-braised venison cuts; braise liquid and any flour thickening unconfirmed.

items.en: Lunch Set (Pizza or Pasta + Salad + Appetizer + Bread + Coffee/Tea)
items.note: Choice of one pizza or pasta from the daily rotation, plus salad, a small appetizer, bread and a hot drink; add ¥300 for one dessert or ¥500 for a two-dessert plate.

items.ja: 肉団子のトマトクリームソース
items.note: A specific lunch-menu meatball dish a blogger reviewed by name and price; meatballs likely bound with breadcrumbs.
A tasting-size half portion, per the shop's own entrance signboard — 一寸 (issun) plays on "just a little bit." Standard wheat-blended soba in a bonito-dashi, wheat-soy tsuyu.

items.en: Cold Soba on a Bamboo Tray
items.note: A diner's review describes a notably rich, sharp (辛目) dipping tsuyu here. Soba blend not confirmed as jūwari (100% buckwheat) or nihachi — assume wheat-blended unless the shop says otherwise; the tsuyu itself is wheat soy sauce either way.

items.en: Cold Soba with Warm Duck Dipping Broth
items.note: Duck simmered into the hot dipping tsuyu, noodles served cold and separate — a reviewer called the noodles here unusually thin and refined. Duck + wheat-soy tsuyu, not for a celiac or vegan diner.

Served at the end of the meal to drink on its own or poured into the leftover dipping tsuyu. The hot water itself is usually just buckwheat starch runoff, but it is customarily mixed into the wheat-soy tsuyu — ask for it separate and unmixed.

A 2024 diner review notes curry is on the menu specifically as an option for people who don't want soba, including kids — exact form (rice or noodle) not confirmed. Curry roux is wheat-thickened and typically meat-stock based.

items.ja: マロンクリームと信州真島産カシスのパンケーキ

items.en: Chestnut Cream & Shinshu Majima Blackcurrant (Cassis) Pancake
items.note: Fluffy Japanese-style pancake topped with chestnut cream and blackcurrant grown in Majima, Nagano. Wheat batter with dairy cream — never gf, not vegan. The shop's own site is now offline; this is drawn from the cafe's 2015 blog and may have changed.

items.ja: 信州りんごのパンケーキ
items.note: Made with red Kōgyoku apples from Miyahara Farm in Chikuma City; same wheat/dairy pancake base as the rest of the pancake menu.

items.ja: ナガノパープルとクリームチーズのマフィン

items.en: Nagano Purple Grape & Cream Cheese Muffin
items.note: Baked muffin studded with Nagano Purple (a seedless grape bred in the prefecture) and cream cheese; historically sold out fast enough that the shop offered to hold one at lunch.

items.ja: 無着色たらこといろいろきのこのスパゲティ

items.note: Wheat pasta tossed with dye-free cod roe and mixed mushrooms — contains fish roe and gluten.

items.en: Prosciutto & Fresh Mushroom Tomato Sauce Pasta

items.ja: 秋鮭とさつまいものクリームソース
items.romaji: Akizake to Satsumaimo no Kuriimu Soosu
items.en: Autumn Salmon & Sweet Potato Cream Sauce Pasta
items.note: Cream-sauce pasta with salmon and sweet potato — dairy cream and wheat pasta.

items.ja: ツナといろいろきのこのペペロンチーノ
items.romaji: Tsuna to Iroiro Kinoko no Peperonchiino
items.note: Garlic-chili oil wheat pasta with canned tuna and mixed mushrooms.

items.ja: 粗挽きソーセージと白いんげん豆のトマトソース　ローズマリー風味
items.romaji: Arabiki Sooseeji to Shiroingenmame no Tomato Soosu Roozumarii Fuumi
items.en: Coarse-Ground Sausage & White Bean Tomato Sauce, Rosemary
items.note: Sausage and white-bean tomato sauce over wheat pasta, rosemary-scented.

items.ja: 北海道産ホタテ貝柱とズッキーニのゴルゴンゾーラ・クリームソース
items.romaji: Hokkaido-san Hotate Kaibashira to Zukkiini no Gorugonzoora Kuriimu Soosu
items.en: Hokkaido Scallop & Zucchini Gorgonzola Cream Sauce Pasta
items.note: Blue-cheese cream sauce with scallops and zucchini over wheat pasta — shellfish and dairy both present.

items.ja: いろいろキノコのカフェ風ビーフストロガノフ（ドリンク付）
items.romaji: Iroiro Kinoko no Kafe-fuu Biifu Sutoroganofu (Dorinku Tsuki)
items.en: Cafe-Style Mixed-Mushroom Beef Stroganoff, with drink included
items.note: The one item with a confirmed price, from a diner's Tabelog review — a cream-and-mushroom beef stroganoff with a drink included. Likely a flour-thickened sauce; definitely not vegan.

items.ja: ケニアの無農薬栽培紅茶
items.note: Straight black tea — vegan as brewed; ask if it's served with milk.
Plain iced tea; ask if a milk or syrup version is offered.

items.en: Curry Plate (this week: okra & chickpea curry)
items.note: This week's plate: オクラとひよこ豆のカレー (okra & chickpea curry) with rice, potato masala, a simmered-beet side, carrot rapé and a soft-boiled egg. The curry base may be plant-based, but soy sauce/wheat seasoning is the default risk, and the egg on top rules out vegan as plated — ask for it without.

items.ja: 夏野菜グリーンカレー（ごはん）
items.en: Summer Vegetable Green Curry with Rice
items.note: A previous week's set main; served with deep-fried tofu in sweet chili sauce and a beet-carrot salad. Curry roux/seasoning is the default wheat risk.

items.en: Deep-Fried Tofu in Sweet Chili Sauce
items.note: Thick fried tofu (atsuage) the cafe describes as "無添加" (no additives) in the sweet-chili dip — ask whether the chili sauce itself contains soy sauce/wheat.

items.ja: 自然栽培ビーツと人参のサラダ
items.romaji: Shizen Saibai Biitsu to Ninjin no Sarada
items.note: A recurring side salad across multiple weeks' lunch sets; dressing ingredients aren't published.

items.ja: 日々ドライカレー（ごはん）
items.en: Cafe Hibi's Dry (Keema-Style) Curry with Rice
items.note: A drier, minced-style curry served with lentil ethnic soup and the beet-carrot salad.

items.ja: レンズ豆のエスニックスープ
items.note: A spiced lentil soup accompanying the dry-curry set; exact seasoning unpublished.
Classic egg-and-milk custard pudding — not vegan; the caramel/garnish isn't confirmed gluten-free.

items.ja: カスタードプリンと自家製メロンシャーベット、バニラアイスクリーム
items.romaji: Kasutaado Purin to Jikasei Meron Shaabetto, Banira Aisukuriimu
items.en: Custard Pudding with Homemade Melon Sherbet & Vanilla Ice Cream
items.note: A combination plate — egg custard and dairy ice cream both rule out vegan.

items.ja: 自家製メロンシャーベットとバニラアイスクリーム
items.romaji: Jikasei Meron Shaabetto to Banira Aisukuriimu
items.en: Homemade Melon Sherbet with Vanilla Ice Cream
items.note: The melon sherbet alone may be dairy-free, but it's plated with dairy vanilla ice cream.
Baked with the cafe's own domestic-wheat flour; flavor rotates (yellow peach & cheese one week, white peach & camembert another) — always wheat, and often dairy-cheese topped.

items.ja: 南高梅と小谷の甘酒のかき氷
items.romaji: Nankou-ume to Otari no Amazake no Kakigoori
items.en: Nanko Plum & Otari Amazake Shaved Ice
items.note: Shaved ice with Nanko-ume plum syrup and amazake (fermented sweet rice) from Otari village. Amazake is naturally gf if made from rice alone — ask about the koji source and any added sweeteners.

items.ja: マスカルポーネプラムのかき氷
items.note: Contains mascarpone cheese — not vegan.
Made with Nagano's own anzu apricot; syrup ingredients not published.

items.ja: コーヒーゼリーティラミスかき氷
items.note: Tiramisu-style shaved ice with coffee jelly and mascarpone, almost certainly with sponge/ladyfinger pieces mixed in — treat as containing wheat and dairy by default.
Currently sourced from Nishimi Coffee (Suzu, Ishikawa); black coffee is naturally gf and vegan, and a decaf option is available.

items.en: Chinese Chimaki Morning Set (sticky rice dumpling with braised pork, egg, pickles)
items.note: A big glutinous-rice dumpling stuffed with braised pork belly, wrapped and steamed in a bamboo leaf, plus a boiled egg and pickles — unusual for a Nagano cafe morning menu; the rice itself is wheat-free but the braising liquid is standard soy sauce, so don't call it GF.

items.ja: トーストセット（チーズ）
items.note: Toasted bread with melted cheese and mayonnaise — standard wheat toast.

items.ja: トーストセット（バター）
items.note: Plain buttered toast, the simpler of the two toast-set options.

items.en: "Bonchi Pao" — Taiwan-style steamed bun with braised pork
items.note: A fluffy steamed bun (gua bao-style) filled with soy-braised pork belly, served with a side of beans — the bun itself is wheat.
A glazed wheat-flour lemon pound cake, one of the shop's most-photographed sweets.
Part of the rotating cake-case selection; standard baked cheesecake on a flour base.

Roasted brown rice (genmai) steeped and mixed with steamed milk — the shop names it as pure roasted rice, not a barley grain-coffee, so it reads as wheat-free; the milk is dairy unless you ask for a plant substitute.
Unsweetened hot coffee with milk — wheat-free, dairy-based.
The owner is noted for careful brewing; black coffee is wheat-free, ask before adding milk for vegan.

items.ja: ルイボスティー（アイス）
items.note: Caffeine-free herbal tea, naturally wheat-free and plant-based.

A well-known Nagano oyaki brand, named for the region's Jomon-era farmhouse roots. Dough is wheat- or wheat-buckwheat-blend based; filling (often nozawana greens, sometimes vegetable or meat) isn't specified here — ask which filling is on offer and whether it's vegan.
Deep-fried, panko-breaded croquette filled with Nagano beef and mashed potato — breadcrumbs and beef rule out both gf and vegan.

Deep-fried pounded rice cake wrapped in nori and typically brushed with soy sauce (the "isobe" style). The mochi itself is rice, but the soy-sauce glaze is the usual wheat risk, and the fryer may be shared with breaded items — ask.

items.ja: 信州りんご　シナノスイート
items.note: A crisp, low-acid apple cultivar bred in Nagano — naturally gluten-free and vegan whole fruit.

items.ja: 八幡屋磯五郎　七味唐辛子
items.note: The famous Zenkoji-district shichimi blend (see the Yawataya Isogoro shop entry), sold here as an add-on souvenir. Naturally wheat-free ingredients, but no allergen statement confirmed at this shop.

items.ja: プレミアム濃厚ミルク
items.note: Dairy soft-serve — naturally gluten-free, not vegan.
Nagano's grilled skewered pounded-rice cake with a sweet walnut- or sesame-miso glaze; the glaze is soy-sauce based and the miso may be barley — treat as containing wheat and not vegan by default.
A novelty-named fiery fried-chicken snack; fried and almost certainly soy-marinated and flour-dusted.
A cover charge, not a food item.

items.ja: 世界5大ウイスキー（スコッチ／アイリッシュ／ジャパニーズ／アメリカン／カナディアン）
items.en: The World's Five Great Whiskies — Scotch, Irish, Japanese, American, Canadian
items.note: All five styles typically use a malted-barley or wheat mash. Distillation removes most gluten protein by most food-safety accounts, but flavoring/coloring added after distillation can vary — a curious celiac should ask rather than assume safe. No animal ingredients in straight whiskey, so vegan.

items.ja: 軽食（信州牛コロッケ／フライドチキン／スパイシーチキン）
items.romaji: Keishoku (Shinshu-gyu Korokke / Furaido Chikin / Supaishii Chikin)
items.en: Bar Snacks — Shinshu Beef Croquette / Fried Chicken / Spicy Chicken
items.note: The same fried daytime snacks served as evening bar food alongside whiskey.

items.ja: 濃厚バニラソフトクリーム
items.note: Dairy soft-serve offered as a bar dessert.

items.ja: 軽食付きプラン（要予約・5名様まで）
items.note: A pre-booked (1 week ahead) tasting course for up to 5 guests; content and price are set to the guest's stated budget — no fixed menu is published, so ask the kitchen directly about every course.

Per a diner's Tabelog review, the night bar's compulsory otōshi starter is a daifuku (soft mochi stuffed with sweet anko) that guests may take home — the source of this shop's "daifuku and whiskey" nickname, though it isn't listed on the shop's own published menu. Sourced from a review, not the shop's own copy — treat as provisional. The rice-mochi wrapper is wheat-free; anko filling is usually vegan but confirm.

items.ja: モーニングセット　たまごのオープンサンド
items.romaji: Mooningu Setto — Tamago no Oopun Sando
items.note: One of two morning-set choices, open-faced egg salad on bread; standard wheat toast base.

items.ja: モーニングセット　カリッとバターはちみつトースト
items.romaji: Mooningu Setto — Karitto Bataa Hachimitsu Toosuto
items.en: Morning Set — Crispy Butter Honey Toast
items.note: Thick toast finished crisp with butter and honey — wheat and dairy.
Pressed, grilled sandwich — wheat bread; filling varies.
Curry-filled bread roll, oven-baked rather than fried, but still a wheat bun with roux-thickened curry filling.
Wheat-pastry apple pie, part of the kissaten-style dessert case.

items.ja: プリン（サンデーレトロプリン）
items.en: "Sunday Retro Pudding" — firm old-style custard pudding
items.note: The shop's signature dessert, made deliberately firm in the old-fashioned kissaten style — pick cinnamon or Yawataya Isogoro shichimi (Nagano chili spice blend) as a topping. Custard puddings are usually flour-free but not confirmed; egg and dairy rule out vegan regardless.

items.ja: 季節限定　珈琲ゼリー　はちみつ×ホイップ
items.romaji: Kisetsu Gentei — Koohii Zerii, Hachimitsu x Hoippu
items.en: Seasonal Coffee Jelly with Honey & Whipped Cream
items.note: House drip coffee set into jelly, topped with 100-year-old Omachi dairy Matsuda Milk's whipped cream and honey (red-bean topping also offered); the jelly itself is wheat-free, but whipped dairy cream and honey rule out vegan.

items.ja: 本日のストレートコーヒー
items.note: The house specialty — a daily-changing single-origin pour from a Tokyo roaster; one reviewer's tasting note compared it to aged whisky. Black coffee is wheat-free and plant-based.
Matcha whisked with steamed dairy milk — wheat-free, not vegan unless a plant-milk swap is confirmed.
Spiced black tea with milk — the spice mix isn't published so a trace-malt ingredient can't be ruled out; dairy-based regardless.
Caffeine-free herbal red tea, naturally wheat-free and plant-based.
Standard 二八 (nihachi) blend — 80% buckwheat, 20% wheat flour as a binder. Tsuyu is wheat soy sauce.

The house special: 十割 (jūwari), 100% buckwheat, grown on the Togakushi highland — one of Japan's three great soba regions, hand-formed into bocchi-mori: rinsed cold, gathered into small coiled bundles (bocchi), five bundles arranged on one woven zaru. Even fully buckwheat, it shares boiling water/boards with wheat noodles and the tsuyu is wheat soy sauce — never truly celiac-safe. Priced here as a 5-bocchi serving.
Soba with seasonal vegetables, likely in a hot dashi broth. Same wheat/cross-contamination caveats as any soba here.

items.en: Hot Soba with Matsushiro Mountain Yam
items.note: Hot broth soba topped with grated nagaimo mountain yam grown in Matsushiro, a Nagano-city district. Broth is dashi-based.
Soba topped with tempura — batter is wheat flour, on top of the soba's own wheat exposure.
Hot soba with duck and Japanese leek in the broth.
Soba with wild mushrooms foraged from Mt. Togakushi. Vegan status depends on whether the broth is kombu-mushroom only or the shop's usual bonito dashi — ask.

Buckwheat flour kneaded with hot water into a thick dumpling/paste — no wheat in the dumpling itself, unlike noodles. But it's typically dipped in the same wheat soy sauce tsuyu or a savory sauce, so ask what it's served with before calling it GF.
A fiercely pungent local daikon variety, grated as a soba condiment in place of (or alongside) wasabi — a Togakushi-soba signature. Likely just daikon plus a little soy sauce; ask.
Sticky grated yam, usually loosened with a little dashi and soy sauce — ask about the seasoning liquid.
Deep-fried mixed vegetable (and possibly seafood) fritter in wheat batter — not GF. Vegan status depends on whether shrimp is in the mix; not confirmed.
Miso paste grilled with whole buckwheat groats stirred in — a classic soba-shop nibble with sake. Miso can be barley-based (麦味噌); not confirmed here.
Japanese rolled omelette, usually sweetened with dashi stock mixed into the egg — check for soy sauce/wheat in the dashi. Contains egg either way.
Kamaboko fish cake, sliced and served with wasabi and soy sauce. Kamaboko commonly uses wheat starch as a binder, and it's fish — not GF, not vegan.
Tofu gently warmed in the starchy buckwheat cooking water, usually finished with a soy-based dip. Ask about the dipping sauce.
Chilled tofu topped with scallion, ginger and usually bonito flakes — assume bonito unless told otherwise (not vegan); soy sauce drizzle likely (ask for GF).
Shinshu's own speciality: thin-sliced raw horse, served with grated ginger/garlic and soy sauce for dipping — the soy sauce is the GF issue.
Raw horse liver, same soy-sauce dip as basashi.
House curry made with horse meat — wheat-thickened roux, meat-based.
Nagano-region beef, lightly seared outside and raw within, served with a soy-based dip.
Chef's choice sashimi, served with soy sauce.
Whole river char, grilled with just salt — no soy sauce or batter, genuinely wheat-free as a dish. Still confirm nothing else touched the grill, and it's fish, not vegan.
Mixed tempura platter, wheat batter throughout — not GF. Vegan depends on the day's mix (shrimp is common).

items.ja: 蕎麦の実とあんずアイス
items.note: Dairy ice cream studded with whole buckwheat groats and Nagano apricot (anzu) — the groats themselves are wheat-free, but confirm no other mix-ins; contains dairy, not vegan.

items.ja: 戸隠蕎麦と季節の料理コース
items.romaji: Togakushi Soba to Kisetsu no Ryōri Kōsu
items.section: コース / Course Menus (reserve 3 days ahead)
items.note: Multi-course chef's menu built around the house jūwari Togakushi soba plus seasonal small plates — expect the same wheat/dashi exposure as the rest of the menu across every course.

items.ja: 戸隠蕎麦と大将の特別料理コース
items.romaji: Togakushi Soba to Taishō no Tokubetsu Ryōri Kōsu
items.section: コース / Course Menus (reserve 3 days ahead)
items.note: The top-tier omakase course, chef's choice throughout, built around Togakushi soba — not GF or vegan-adaptable without extensive advance discussion.

items.en: Junsai Water Shield with Grated Mountain Yam
items.note: Junsai (a slippery aquatic plant, texture is the point per the ryokan's own copy) over grated tororo yam; likely dressed with soy-based sauce — ask. Note the location: Masuya is a ryokan in Yudanaka Onsen, Yamanouchi Town, about 22 km from Nagano City — this is a stay, not an evening out from the station.

items.ja: 旬菜色々（稚鮎の煮浸し、芋茎の辛子和え、ホッキ貝わさび和え、トマトもずく寄せ、杏）
items.en: Seasonal Appetizer Assortment — simmered baby ayu, mustard-dressed imokara stems, surf clam with wasabi, tomato-mozuku, apricot
items.note: A five-bite assortment including simmered young ayu river fish (soy-based nimono) and shellfish — not GF (soy sauce) and not vegan (fish/shellfish).

items.ja: 信州サーモン岩魚の昆布〆
items.en: Kombu-cured Shinshu Salmon and Iwana Char Sashimi
items.note: Two of Nagano's own farmed fish, Shinshu salmon and mountain-stream iwana char, cured with kombu; served with soy sauce for dipping unless requested otherwise.

items.ja: 志賀高原の清流で養殖されました鮎のひと口寿司
items.romaji: Shiga Kougen no Seiryuu de Youshoku Saremashita Ayu no Hitokuchi Sushi
items.en: Bite-size Sushi of Ayu Sweetfish Farmed in the Shiga Kogen Clear Streams
items.note: Sushi rice is seasoned with rice vinegar and usually sugar/mirin (mirin can contain wheat-derived alcohol) — not GF; fish-based, not vegan.

Served as a small in-course cleanser, not a full bowl. Whether it's 十割 (100% buckwheat) or blended is not stated, and the dipping tsuyu is standard wheat-soy-based regardless — never treat any soba course as GF. Vegan status depends on whether the tsuyu carries bonito dashi.
Thin-sliced local mountain char swished in broth at the table; broth base and dipping sauce not detailed — ask before assuming GF.

items.ja: 信州牛のサーロインステーキ
items.note: Branded Nagano beef; steak sauce may be soy/wheat-based — ask for tamari or a plain salt finish.

items.ja: 百合根白玉の蕎麦の実あんかけ
items.en: Lily-bulb Rice Dumplings with Buckwheat-groat Thickened Sauce
items.note: The ankake sauce is almost always wheat-starch or wheat-flour thickened even though the groats floating in it are buckwheat — do not read "蕎麦の実" as gluten-free.

items.ja: てんぷら（北信濃産アスパラ、山椒塩で）
items.en: Tempura of North-Shinano Asparagus, with Sansho Pepper Salt
items.note: Standard tempura batter is wheat flour — not GF. Sansho-salt dip (no soy) may make this the vegan-friendliest course if the batter itself is egg-free — ask.
Rice porridge with foraged sansai mountain greens; broth is very likely dashi-based (bonito) and possibly soy-seasoned — ask on both counts.

items.ja: 自家製トマトのシャーベット
items.note: Tomato sorbet — naturally wheat- and dairy-free as described; still worth a quick ask given the shared kitchen.

items.ja: 大岩魚のしゃぶしゃぶ
items.note: Same dish as the course-included iwana shabu-shabu but as a larger stand-alone order.

items.en: Shinshu Beef Steamed in Hot-spring Water
items.note: Local specialty technique — beef steamed using the ryokan's own onsen source water; seasoning/sauce not detailed.

items.en: Iwana Bone Sake (grilled fish warmed in hot sake)
items.section: 別注料理 (À la carte, drinks)
items.note: A whole grilled iwana steeped in hot sake — traditionally just fish and sake, so naturally wheat-free; not vegan.

sources: https://huuhu-gourmet.com/2025/08/25/長野駅から徒歩1分！人気「みそ家」のアクセス完/

items.note: The house bowl since 1959 and the only thing this 12-seat counter has ever served. Shinshu miso is a rice-koji (not barley) miso, aged for depth — sweeter and more aromatic than a Hokkaido-style miso ramen. Ordinary yellow wheat noodles, bean sprouts, one thick chashu slab. Wheat noodles and an undocumented tare mean this is not GF regardless of the miso itself.

items.ja: 味噌ちゃあしゅうめん
items.en: Shinshu Miso Ramen with Extra Chashu
items.note: Same miso bowl with four slices of pork chashu instead of one.
The miso base with seasoned ground meat stirred in for heat and texture.

items.ja: 辛味噌ちゃあしゅうめん
items.en: Spicy Miso Ramen with Extra Chashu
items.note: Spicy miso bowl with three extra chashu slices.

items.en: Miso Ramen with Stone-Milled Nagano-Wheat Noodles
items.note: Pay a small upcharge and the noodles switch to ones stone-milled from Nagano-grown wheat — thick, seriously chewy, and dark enough to look like soba in the bowl. It is the house's real reason for existing, but it is still wheat, just a different (and better) one; not a GF option.

items.en: Stone-Milled Noodle Ramen with Extra Chashu
items.note: Stone-milled noodle bowl with four chashu slices.

items.en: Spicy Miso Ramen with Stone-Milled Noodles
items.note: Spicy version with the stone-milled Nagano-wheat noodle.

items.ja: 石臼辛味噌ちゃあしゅう
items.en: Spicy Miso Ramen, Stone-Milled Noodles, Extra Chashu
items.note: The most-loaded bowl on the board: spicy miso, stone-milled noodle, three extra chashu slices.
Noodles served separately from a concentrated hot miso dipping broth — dunk and slurp. Same wheat noodle and undocumented tare as the ramen bowls.
Tsukemen with the stone-milled Nagano-wheat noodle upgrade.
More of the standard yellow wheat noodle in the same bowl.
Extra-portion surcharge specifically for the stone-milled Nagano-wheat noodle.
Fermented/seasoned bamboo shoots (menma) — usually soy-seasoned; confirm for soy/wheat and dashi.
Add three extra slices of the braised pork chashu to any bowl.
Plain boiled egg, not marinated — likely GF on its own, but confirm no seasoning brush; contains egg so not vegan.

Plain steamed rice — naturally wheat-free and animal-free on its own, and the only such thing in the building. Order it unseasoned, and be aware the counter, scoop and every surface around it belong to a wheat-noodle kitchen: survival food, not a safe meal.
Standard Japanese barley-malt beer — contains gluten.

The most-ordered bowl. Made with 安養寺みそ (Anyoji miso), a rice-koji miso from Saku aged over two years — far longer than an ordinary miso — for a dark, almost tannic depth rather than a bright salty hit. Seasoned pork mince is stirred through the whole bowl rather than laid on top. Medium-thick straight wheat noodles; not GF.
Loaded version of the house bowl — extra chashu and a seasoned egg on top of the pork-mince miso soup.

The kitchen's non-miso register: a Wakayama-produced tamari shoyu with a quiet sweetness, sliced chashu, menma, nori and a wedge of onion. Trap: Japanese tamari is brewed differently from Western wheat-free tamari and is NOT reliably gluten-free here — no such claim is made — and the noodles are wheat regardless.
Loaded tamari-shoyu bowl with extra thick-cut chashu, a marinated egg and greens.
Miso ramen enriched with a seafood (niboshi/dried-fish) stock behind it — a fishier, more savoury take on the house miso than the pork-mince version.

items.ja: 特製魚介味噌らぅめん
items.note: Loaded seafood-miso bowl with extra chashu and egg.
The lightest bowl on the board — a clear, golden chicken (Shiretoko-brand chicken) shio broth rather than miso, with sliced chicken chashu. Wheat noodles still apply; not GF.
A niboshi (dried sardine) stock layered into a pork-bone (tonkotsu) base — fishier and funkier than a plain tonkotsu bowl.

items.ja: 家系豚骨醤油らぅめん
items.note: A Yokohama Iekei-style bowl — thick chewy noodles, a creamy pork-bone-and-soy broth, nori, spinach and chashu. Wheat soy sauce and wheat noodles throughout.

items.ja: つけそば 濃厚知床鶏
items.note: Cold noodles dipped into a thick, concentrated hot chicken broth — Shiretoko-brand chicken.

items.ja: つけそば 魚介味噌
items.note: Cold noodles dipped into a thick seafood-miso broth.
Sliced braised pork over rice with scallion — the rice itself is GF but the chashu braise is typically soy-based; ask.

Pan-fried pork gyoza served with a Shinshu-miso dipping sauce; confirmed from the shop's mail-order lineup (sold as a home-delivery product), likely also offered in-store. Wheat gyoza wrapper — not GF.

Plain cold soba on a tray with dipping sauce. Buckwheat ratio (jūwari vs nihachi) is not published — assume a wheat-blended noodle. The tsuyu is wheat soy sauce based, and dashi is typically bonito — ask if a plant-based tsuyu exists (unlikely).

items.en: Cold Soba with Hot Duck Dipping Broth
items.note: Cold soba dipped into a hot, duck-fat-rich broth with sliced duck and leek — one of the shop's headline dishes. Wheat-blended noodles and wheat soy sauce broth; duck stock means it's not vegan either.
Cold soba plus a full tempura plate — wheat noodles, wheat-battered tempura, and a shared fryer stack three separate reasons this isn't GF.

Named for Togakushi, one of Japan's three great soba regions — served with grated daikon radish instead of a plain dipping sauce. Still a wheat-blended noodle and soy-based sauce underneath the radish.
The Iizuna-area cousin of Nagano's おしぼりうどん idea — a hot, sharply spicy grated-daikon-juice topping over soba. Not gluten-free for the same noodle/tsuyu reasons.
Plain hot soba in a bonito-dashi broth built on wheat soy sauce.
Hot soba topped with tempura — wheat noodles plus wheat-battered, shared-fryer tempura.

items.en: Hot Soba with Grated Mountain Yam
items.note: Hot soba with grated nagaimo yam stirred in for a slippery texture. Yam itself is GF; the noodle and tsuyu are not.

items.en: Hot Soba with Duck and Leek
items.note: Hot soba with sliced duck and leek in the broth — a classic pairing ("nanban" = with leek).
Hot soba loaded with a mix of mushrooms. Mushrooms are naturally GF/vegan-friendly but the noodle and dashi/tsuyu are not.

items.en: Grilled Dry Soba on a Board
items.note: The shop's own original — raw soba noodles grilled dry on a wire net and served with a scallion miso for dipping, no broth at all. Still wheat-blended noodle; the miso dip may be barley miso and its dashi content is unstated.
Sliced raw soba dough served like sashimi, dipped in the regular soba tsuyu — a novelty way to taste the noodle itself before cooking. Same wheat/soy caveats as the rest of the board.

items.ja: 馬刺し 赤身の最高峰 ヒレ
items.note: Raw horse sashimi (basashi), a genuine Nagano/Shinshu specialty, served with grated ginger/garlic and soy sauce. The meat itself is naturally GF; the dipping soy sauce is wheat-based — ask for a GF-safe soy or skip it.

items.ja: 馬刺し ヘルシー赤身
items.note: A leaner, lower-fat basashi cut. Same soy-dip caveat as the fillet version.
Tempura over rice with a sweet soy glaze — wheat batter, wheat sauce, shared fryer.
Tempura plate with rice, miso soup and pickles.
Boiled, salted soybeans in the pod — naturally GF and vegan; the safest order in the house alongside plain rice.
Chilled tofu with toppings (usually katsuobushi bonito flakes and soy sauce) — ask for a plain version without bonito or soy for a vegan/GF-friendlier bite.
Standard soy-marinated, flour-dusted fried chicken; not GF and not vegan.
Nagano's signature salt-pickled leaf-mustard, topped with bonito flakes here — not vegan because of the katsuobushi; confirm no soy/wheat seasoning for GF.

items.ja: 西之門 善光寺 純米吟醸 300ml
items.note: Local Nagano sake named for Zenkoji Temple — rice-based, naturally GF; some sake is fined with animal products, so ask if strict vegan matters.

items.ja: リンゴジュース 秋映
items.note: Single-variety apple juice from the Akibae cultivar, one of three Nagano-bred apple juices on the drinks list — naturally GF and vegan.

The cheapest item on the board and reportedly one of the least expensive station-platform sobas anywhere in Japan. Noodles are a wheat-blended machine noodle (not jūwari), and this counter runs soba and udon through the SAME boiling pot — cross-contamination either way. Broth is a fish-dashi, wheat-soy-sauce tsuyu, slightly stronger/darker in the Hokushin (north Nagano) style the shop says it preserves.
Same broth, same shared pot as the soba — the udon itself is 100% wheat.
Topped with a fritter (typically a kakiage-style tempura) — wheat batter on top of the wheat noodle and wheat-soy tsuyu.
A visiting blogger called this generously topped with mushrooms and seaweed for the price — good value, but still wheat-blend noodles and dashi tsuyu.
A raw egg cracked into the hot broth, named for its resemblance to a full moon. Contains egg — not vegan.
Topped with simmered sansai (foraged mountain vegetables — usually warabi/zenmai fern shoots). Vegetables themselves are plant-based but simmered in a soy-dashi seasoning — ask.
Topped with a sweet-simmered aburaage fried-tofu pouch, soy- and sugar-braised — confirm no bonito dashi in the braise for a vegan order.
The classic order at this stand — a fried shrimp tempura piece on top. Shellfish plus wheat batter plus wheat noodle.
Topped with rehydrated wakame seaweed — naturally plant-based on its own, but the broth beneath it is dashi/wheat-soy based.
One of the shop's two headline items alongside the tempura soba — sliced beef or pork simmered in a sweet-soy sauce over udon.

items.ja: 肉チートロそば・うどん
items.note: The stand's viral specialty — meat udon/soba with cheese melted in ("チートロ" blends チーズ cheese with とろける "melting"). It has been called out in "must-try station soba" rankings. Dairy plus wheat noodle plus wheat-soy broth.

items.ja: チートロスペシャルそば・うどん
items.note: The everything-bowl version: egg, a kakiage-style fritter, meat, cheese, onion and scallion all piled onto the wheat noodle base, with black pepper available on request.
A Japanese curry-roux broth over udon (soba can be substituted on request). Curry roux is wheat-thickened — not GF, and confirm no meat stock for vegan.

items.ja: 冷やしかけそば・うどん
items.note: Cold-broth summer version of the basic bowl, available seasonally.

items.ja: 冷やし山菜そば・うどん
items.note: Cold summer bowl topped with sansai mountain vegetables.
Add a second helping of noodles to the same bowl of broth. The shop notes this isn't always available if the broth is running low, since it's a fast-turnover platform counter.
Nagano's own fried chicken — a whole marinated thigh dusted in flour or potato starch and deep-fried; the marinade is wheat soy sauce and the coating is starch/flour, so not GF.

items.section: 信州マタギ鍋 / Matagi Hunter Hot Pots
items.note: One of the shop's 'matagi' (traditional mountain-hunter) hot pots — wild boar simmered with vegetables in a soy-based broth; genuinely unusual game outside Nagano's mountain districts.

items.section: 信州マタギ鍋 / Matagi Hunter Hot Pots
items.note: The most exotic of the shop's hunter hot pots — wild bear meat simmered in a savoury soy broth; a genuine Shinshu matagi (hunter) dish, not a novelty add-on.

items.section: 信州マタギ鍋 / Matagi Hunter Hot Pots
items.note: "Sakura" (cherry blossom) is the traditional Japanese euphemism for horse meat — the same Shinshu specialty behind raw basashi sashimi, but here simmered in a soy-miso broth alongside the shop's other matagi hunter hot pots rather than served raw. Priced in the same ¥4,389–5,390 band as the other nabe.
Raw deer meat sashimi, listed alongside the shop's Shinshu salmon as a regional specialty — the meat itself is naturally wheat-free but ask about the dipping sauce, which is normally wheat soy sauce.

Nagano farmhouse food — a wheat-or-buckwheat dough wrapper stuffed with salt-pickled nozawana leaf-mustard greens, then steamed; oyaki dough is wheat by default unless a shop states otherwise, so treat this as not GF.
Three different oyaki fillings on one plate — same wheat-dough caveat as the single nozawana oyaki; fillings vary and aren't itemised.

items.ja: 昔ながらの野沢菜漬け
items.note: The region's iconic leaf-mustard pickle, made the old way — plain salt-curing is naturally wheat-free; ask whether any dashi/bonito was used in the brine before calling it vegan.

items.en: Nozawana Pickle Over Rice in Green Tea Broth
items.note: Rice doused in hot green tea or dashi broth and topped with nozawana pickle — confirm whether the broth is plain tea or a bonito dashi.

One of Japan's three great soba styles — traditionally served in small bocchi-mori coils on a woven zaru basket. Even here, the tsuyu dipping sauce is regular wheat soy sauce and the same water/boards handle wheat udon, so never call soba GF.

items.en: Touji Soba (basket-dipped soba in hot broth)
items.note: A Hakuba/mountain-village style — a basket of soba is dipped into a simmering pot of vegetable-and-meat broth at the table, then the broth is drunk at the end. The broth itself is soy-seasoned, so not GF even if the noodles were jūwari.

items.section: 長野の郷土料理 / Nagano Local Dishes
items.note: A rarity among Japanese pickles — Kiso-region turnip greens fermented with wild lactic bacteria and NO salt at all, unlike almost every other tsukemono; naturally wheat-free and plant-based as long as no soy sauce is added at plating.

items.ja: 信州そば粉の揚げだし豆腐
items.en: Fried Tofu Dusted in Buckwheat Flour, in Dashi Broth
items.section: 長野の郷土料理 / Nagano Local Dishes
items.note: A local twist on agedashi tofu — coated in soba-ko (buckwheat flour) instead of the usual wheat starch, which is promising, but the dashi broth it sits in is bonito-based and usually seasoned with wheat soy sauce, so it isn't a safe GF/vegan bet without asking.

items.section: 長野の郷土料理 / Nagano Local Dishes
items.note: Sobagaki is pure kneaded buckwheat paste with no wheat binder, grilled — the dumpling itself is the closest thing to GF soba on this menu, but the dipping sauce is standard wheat soy sauce, so ask before assuming it's safe.

items.ja: 信州ソーセージの盛り合わせ
items.section: 長野の郷土料理 / Nagano Local Dishes
items.note: A plate of local sausages — commercial sausage casings and binders commonly include wheat, so treat as not GF unless confirmed otherwise.

items.section: 信州の食事 / Shinshu Rice Dishes
items.note: A Nagano-area katsudon variant — the panko-breaded cutlet is dipped in a savoury Worcester-style sauce over rice instead of the usual egg-and-dashi; wheat panko and wheat sauce both rule out GF.

items.section: 信州の食事 / Shinshu Rice Dishes
items.note: A regional specialty from Ina, southern Nagano — steamed wheat noodles stir-fried with lamb or mutton and cabbage in a soy-based sauce; despite the name it's unrelated to ramen broth. Wheat noodles and lamb rule out both GF and vegan.

items.ja: 北アルプスのおぼろ豆腐
items.en: Soft-Set "Oboro" Tofu, made with North Alps spring water
items.section: 長野の郷土料理 / Nagano Local Dishes
items.note: Freshly set, unpressed tofu made with mountain spring water — the tofu itself is naturally wheat-free and plant-based, but it's almost always served with a soy-sauce or ponzu dip, so ask before calling the whole dish safe.

items.ja: 信州福味鶏のやみつき揚げ
items.section: 信州の揚げ物 / Shinshu Fried Dishes
items.note: A branded Nagano chicken (Fukumidori) done as standard karaage — flour/starch-dusted and deep-fried, so not GF; the fryer is shared with other breaded items on this long menu.
Fried rice finished with fresh grated wasabi — the rice itself is fine, but fried rice at this kind of izakaya is normally seasoned with soy sauce, so ask before assuming GF or vegan.

items.en: Fresh Real Wasabi Root, grated to order (Azumino)
items.note: Whole fresh wasabi rhizome from Azumino, one of Japan's premier wasabi-growing valleys, hand-grated at the table — plain wasabi root is naturally wheat-free and plant-based; this is real wasabi, not the reconstituted horseradish paste served elsewhere.

items.section: 信州の家畜料理 / Shinshu Livestock Dishes
items.note: Shinshu-gyu beef simmered tableside in the classic sukiyaki sweet soy-and-mirin sauce (warishita) — the sauce is wheat soy sauce by default, so not GF.

items.ja: 信州蕎麦の蜂蜜アイス
items.note: Dairy ice cream flavoured with roasted buckwheat (sobacha) and honey — the buckwheat here is a flavouring stirred into a milk base, not a wheat-containing dessert, but it isn't confirmed additive-free; dairy rules out vegan regardless.

items.ja: 蔵出し原酒「大雪渓」正壱合
items.en: Unfiltered Sake Straight from the Cask — "Daisekkei" brand (1 gō)
items.section: 信州の地酒 / Nagano Local Sake
items.note: Sake is brewed from rice and naturally wheat-free; Daisekkei is a well-known brewery from Otari village at the foot of the Northern Alps.

items.ja: 長野全69蔵の地酒 全銘柄（精選）
items.romaji: Nagano Zen 69-gura no Jizake — Zen Meigara (Sensen)
items.en: "All Brands" Selection — one cup from any of Nagano's ~69 breweries
items.section: 信州の地酒 / Nagano Local Sake
items.note: The shop's headline conceit — a printed list running to roughly 70 Nagano breweries by name (真澄, 大信州, 佐久の花, 水尾, 岩清水, 七笑 and dozens more), any one poured for a flat price. Plain sake is rice-brewed and naturally GF/vegan.

items.ja: お造り（信州サーモン、馬刺し）
items.en: Sashimi Plate — Nagano Salmon & Horse Sashimi
items.section: 宴会コース / Banquet Course dish
items.note: The course's raw course pairs farmed Shinshu salmon with basashi (raw horse meat), a genuine Nagano speciality served with grated ginger/garlic and soy — the meat and fish are naturally GF, but the soy dip on the side is not.

items.section: 宴会コース / Banquet Course dish
items.note: Slow-braised pork belly and daikon radish in a soy-mirin simmering liquid — standard wheat soy sauce.

items.section: 宴会コース / Banquet Course dish
items.note: Grilled skewers included in every banquet course — exact contents and glaze aren't published; ask whether it's a plain-salt or soy-glazed skewer.

items.section: 宴会コース / Banquet Course dish
items.note: Standard wheat-battered, deep-fried tempura as a course course — not GF; ask what's inside for vegan.

items.section: 宴会コース / Banquet Course dish

The shop's second most-mentioned dish across reviews — a genuine Shinshu specialty, thin-sliced raw horse served with grated ginger/garlic and soy sauce. The meat is naturally wheat-free; only the soy dip is a GF concern.
A winter-standard simmered pot of fish cakes, daikon, konnyaku and eggs in a dashi-soy broth — the broth is wheat soy sauce and fish cakes typically contain wheat starch as a binder.

A Shinshu home-style pickle of many vegetables (daikon, cucumber, eggplant, ginger etc.) finely diced and mixed with a soy-based marinade — a reviewer's favourite order here; the soy marinade is the GF concern.
Whole small river loach, flour-dusted and deep-fried — one of the "beta" (classic, expected) Shinshu izakaya dishes reviewers note this shop keeps on the menu; not GF.

items.en: Grilled Eggplant with Sweet Miso Glaze

items.en: Round Eggplant with Spicy Fermented Miso
items.note: Nagano's round eggplant variety, served hot with a spicy tekka-miso topping (miso simmered with sesame oil and chili) — a reviewer specifically praised the miso's sweetness against the hot eggplant. Miso grain not confirmed.
Cold or grilled tofu with a scallion-miso topping — tofu itself is fine, miso grain composition not confirmed.
Maitake mushrooms — Nagano grows a large share of Japan's cultivated mushrooms — pan-fried in butter; likely finished with a splash of soy sauce, so ask. Dairy rules out vegan.
Thin brown seaweed in a sweet-vinegar dressing — the vinegar dressing (tosazu) commonly includes a dash of soy sauce or bonito dashi; ask.
Standard miso-soy simmered pork or beef offal — one of the most-mentioned dishes in reviews; not GF.
A second, flatter croquette style named for its resemblance to a straw sandal (waraji) — distinct from the shop's tall signature cheese croquette; same wheat-panko caveat.
Whole small river shrimp, flour-dusted and fried shell-on — a classic Nagano river-food nibble; not GF.

Cucumber buried for months in sake lees until it turns deep brown and boozy — sweet, sharp and genuinely alcoholic. Sake lees itself is rice-based, but commercial narazuke is often made with mirin lees and added seasonings, so confirm before treating it as wheat-free.

Another adventurous offal cut, prized for its distinct crunch. Grilled on the same charcoal as everything else.
Grilled intestine, ordered here as a repeat/extra round by a regular customer — a sign it's one of the better sellers.

Ground meat (chicken or pork) formed onto a skewer and grilled — the shop's self-described signature, usually ordered last. Binders in tsukune are typically egg and a starch/panko — assume wheat unless confirmed otherwise, and the tare glaze if used is wheat soy.
Chicken thigh alternated with leek on the skewer — mentioned by a reviewer but without a listed price. Standard tare/shio question applies.
Grilled chicken heart, another item called out by a visiting reviewer without a price attached.
Pork or beef offal slow-simmered in a miso-and-soy broth with vegetables — a standard izakaya comfort dish. Soy sauce and likely miso (barley risk unconfirmed) rule out GF.
Used generically by reviewers for the shop's grilled chicken skewers alongside the offal-focused ones — cut and seasoning per skewer not itemized beyond what's listed here.
A malt-based beer-flavored soft drink mixed with shochu — contains barley malt, not GF.
Shochu, soda and lemon — shochu is often distilled and GF depending on base grain, but not confirmed here; ask about the base spirit.

The house's top-billed pizza — imported buffalo mozzarella, a sauce that keeps the local tomatoes' texture rather than pureeing it smooth, on a Shinshu-wheat-flour Napoli crust. Wheat crust and dairy cheese.

Prices sit well above a normal soba shop because this is a small hand-made operation, not a lunch counter.
